bugLogs.title: Product image missing alternative text
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open a product detail page on the e‑commerce site.
2. Locate the main product image displayed.
3. Use browser developer tools to inspect the element.
4. Observe that the has no alt attribute, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title, and no role="presentation".
bugLogs.expected_behavior: All elements must provide a text alternative via a descriptive alt attribute, or be marked as decorative with alt="" and role="presentation" (or equivalent).
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The element lacks an alt attribute, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, and role overrides.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add a meaningful alt attribute, e.g., . If the image is purely decorative, use alt="" and role="presentation" instead.

bugLogs.title: Numeric input missing an accessible label
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Navigate to the page containing the quantity selector.
2. Locate the <input type="number" value="1" min="1" max="10"> element.
3. Use a screen reader or accessibility inspection tool to check for an associated label.
4. Observe that the input has no <label>, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or placeholder.
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Every form control must have a programmatically determinable label (via a visible <label>, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or placeholder) so that its purpose is announced by assistive technologies.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The numeric input lacks any associated label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or placeholder, violating WCAG 3.3.2.
bugLogs.suggested_fix:
Add an explicit label element and associate it with the input using the for/id attributes, e.g.,
<label for="quantity">Quantity</label>
<input id="quantity" type="number" value="1" min="1" max="10" style="width:50px;">.
If a visible label cannot be used, provide an appropriate aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute.
